messages.author: 98f82acb94beafe8
messages.subject: pairwise function and RRPP procedure
parts:
Dear all,

I need to use the pairwise function and I think there is a problem with test.type="dist" argument. I have a very big dataset with samples categorized in two main subdivision: males/females (M and F) and continental/island (C and I). I ran the following commands:

# isl=C/I and sex=M/F

lm<-procD.lm(coords~isl*sex, data=gdf)
gp<-interaction(dataset$isl,dataset$sex)
PW <- pairwise(lm, groups = gp)
summary(PW, test.type = "dist", confidence = 0.95, stat.table = TRUE)
summary(PW, test.type = "var", confidence = 0.95, stat.table = TRUE)

The output of the first summary gave no one pairwise statistical significance, but I know from other multivariate tests and from the biology of the species (it's very dimorphic) that it's at least all females-males comparisons should be significant. Conversely, the second summary ("var") give reasonable results, comparable with the outputs of "morphol.disparity" function. Exactly the same situation when size is considered as dependent variable.

I tried some solutions and I found that removing the RRPP procedure (RRPP=F) the outputs were much more comparable with other multivariate tests and consistent with the others analysis (big differeces between sexes and few between islands and continental specimens). 

How it's possible? There is a way to fix this problem? The statistical framework it's still correct despite the correction (RRPP=F) I made?

Thank you very much.

Vasco Avramo

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] pairwise function and RRPP procedure
parts:
Vasco,

Please review your choice of null model (see the help page).  While all male-female vectors might be significantly greater than 0, you tested whether the length of these vectors vary among each other; i.e., your implicit null model had isl and sex as factors, meaning general sexual dimorphism was held constant in the permutation procedure.  (It appears that you might have significant sexual dimorphism, but sexual dimorphism does not vary among levels of isl.)

When you changed RRPP to FALSE, you changed the null model to have just an overall mean.  It is not a problem or something that needs to be fixed.  You just need to be cognizant of the null model you are using.

Best,
Mike

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] pairwise function and RRPP procedure
parts:
Vasco, and everyone,

I encourage everyone to learn to restate the null hypotheses, conditioned on null models.  For example, this simple null hypothesis,

H0: var(means) = 0

is correct, but imprecise.  A more precise way to say to say it is

H0: var(means) | model_i = 0.

This latter way defines the null model used to generate the sampling distributions of the statistic used to evaluate var(means).  The var(means) value will change with different null models.  Is changing RRPP = F correct?  I don’t know.  This means you are testing Ho: var(means) | intercept = 0, which is different than Ho: var(means) | isl + sex = 0.  Is it correct to do that?  It depends on your research question.

There is no simple yes/no way to answer your question, as there is no single way to test the variance among means for factorial models.

Cheers!
Mike
